channel.description: A fresh pick of good news from around the world, every day. Enjoy the read!

item.title: Perseverers and dreamers: the news that captured hearts this week
item.description: Sometimes it seems life gives everyone the same chance, but this week's stories tell a different tale: people who found their own path, no matter how long or winding it was. From a ranch in Montana to the streets of Hull and a film set about a boxer no one saw coming, it's always about perseverance and finding a place where you're seen. item.title: Karl Bushby embraces mother after 28 years walking around the world
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his birthplace Hull after 28 years, where he embraced his tearful mother Angela. The former parachutist set out in 1998 on a 31,000-mile journey through 30 countries, entirely on foot. Along the way, he braved the Darien Gap, was arrested in Russia and swam 170 miles across the Caspian Sea from Kazakhstan to...

item.title: World buys Rothbury Estate for nature restoration
item.description: The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, owned by the Dukes of Northumberland for 800 years since the 13th century, has been purchased by the Wildlife Trusts. More than 25,000 donors from 50 countries raised £30 million together for the 9,400-hectare estate. It will become part of a 40-mile nature corridor between Druridge Bay and an existing nature reserve. The estate is...

item.title: From homeless to Oscar: the story behind Rocky and Sylvester Stallone
item.description: In the nineteen seventies, Sylvester Stallone was homeless in New York and worked long days filleting fish, while audition after audition fell through. His ambition to become an actor was not taken seriously, partly due to partial facial paralysis and a speech impediment resulting from a difficult birth. Frustrated by constantly being cast as a villain, he began writing scripts...

item.title: Satish Kumar wins Future Icons Award for 8,000-mile peace walk
item.description: Country & Town House has announced the winners of the Future Icons Awards 2027 and the Future Icons Power List 2027. Satish Kumar, founder of the Resurgence Trust which publishes The Ecologist, was honoured for walking 8,000 miles through 15 countries in the 1960s without money for peace and for founding Schumacher College in 1991. The awards recognise people, brands...

item.title: European Innovation Council receives €1.8 billion for 2027
item.description: The European Commission has announced €1.8 billion in funding for 2027 through the European Innovation Council (EIC). With this budget, the Commission aims to accelerate the development of breakthrough technologies and support ambitious startups. The goal is to strengthen Europe's position in the global innovation race.

item.title: Vermont Gas brings geothermal heating to affordable homes
item.description: Vermont Gas has struck a groundbreaking deal with geothermal developer Dandelion Energy to equip the 44-unit affordable housing project Riggs Meadow in Hinesburg with geothermal heating and cooling. It is the first project in the US where a utility company owns and manages the installations itself, similar to gas pipelines. Drilling begins in early 2027, with residents able to move...

item.title: Toxic Bangka loris turns out not to have gone extinct after all
item.description: The Bangka slow loris, a primate that had not been scientifically observed since the 1930s and was considered possibly extinct in 2015, has apparently survived all along. Austrian scientists discovered this thanks to a 2022 field guide that referenced the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center on the island of Bangka. This center has been rescuing and reintroducing the animals since 2015,...

item.title: Solar kits transform disaster relief
item.description: Solar kits are bringing a new approach to disaster relief. According to The Optimist Daily, this form of solar energy is changing the way aid is organized and delivered after disasters.

item.title: Erik's Ranch in Montana: autistic guides and wranglers welcome guests
item.description: At Erik's Ranch & Retreats in Montana, near Yellowstone National Park, autistic people work as concierges, guides, wranglers and cooks. Many of them also live on the 230-hectare property. Founder Kathryn Nordberg started the initiative in 2014 out of concern for the future of her autistic son Erik. The cabins are specially designed for neurodivergent guests: calm colors, soundproof doors...

item.title: Butterfly wings as basis for safe paint
item.description: Researchers at Northeastern University are looking to butterflies to develop safer paint and glitter without harmful chemical pigments. They are investigating 'structural colour', where microscopic structures reflect light, as seen in butterfly wings and peacock feathers. item.title: Chocolate from Reading, healing coral and free publishing across Europe
item.description: Early November shows that science doesn't only happen in laboratories, but also comes to life in unexpected places. A student makes a chocolate bar from entirely British soil, researchers discover that damaged coral can heal through simple contact, and European scientists gain more room to share their work for free. item.title: Open Research Europe expands free publishing to 11 countries
item.description: Researchers from 11 European countries can now publish free of charge via Open Research Europe (ORE), the European Commission's open access platform. This follows an expansion of the initiative, giving more scientists in Europe access to publishing without having to pay publication fees.

item.title: Great Terns Return to British South Coast After Bird Flu
item.description: Thanks to targeted nature conservation, great terns have reclaimed a colony on England's south coast, three years after bird flu wiped out the population entirely. Little terns, ringed plovers, common terns and oystercatchers also increased in numbers thanks to the same conservation work by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB). item.title: Keys, puzzle pieces and salty waves: the good news from early November
item.description: These days show how people build things in very different ways: a trade, a bond with family, or a record at sea. From a school workshop in Houston to a swimming journey along the entire California coast, it's always about perseverance and doing something for another person. item.title: Personalized brain therapy achieves 68 percent remission in PTSD
item.description: A personalized form of brain therapy results in remission for 68 percent of people with PTSD. This figure is cited in a report from The Optimist Daily, though further details about the precise mechanism, study design, or researchers involved are lacking. The news is presented as a positive development in mental health care and technology.

item.title: Brazil's Pantanal National Park Significantly Expanded
item.description: Brazilian environmental authorities have expanded the Pantanal Matogrossense National Park by more than 25%: from 523 square miles to 185 additional square miles, roughly equivalent to adding the American Redwoods National Park. The expansion protects the Pantanal, the world's largest flooded grasslands and one of the richest and most vulnerable biomes on Earth. It is home to 463 bird species,...

item.title: Jigsaw puzzle of castle brings granddaughter closer to taciturn grandfather
item.description: Filmmaker Ora DeKornfeld made the documentary The Grandfather Puzzle to get closer to her 99-year-old grandfather, who never wanted to talk about his life in Hungary as a baron. She photographed the castle where he grew up and had a jigsaw puzzle made from it. During her visit, she was welcomed in the small town as a returning baroness, but...

item.title: Catherine Breed becomes first to swim entire California coast
item.description: Long-distance swimmer Catherine Breed is the first person to swim the entire California coastline: 900 miles in 111 days. She started on July 1 at the Oregon-California border and completed the journey on October 19, passing the Mexico border roughly 3 miles offshore to avoid pollution from the Tijuana River. item.title: Students open auto repair shop to the public in Houston
item.description: An auto repair shop run by students has opened in Houston's Fifth Ward. The initiative comes from the Barbara Jordan Career Center, part of Houston Independent School District, which aims to create employment and internship opportunities for students in high-demand trades. The center serves 12 school campuses and more than 1,200 students. Every Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.,...

item.title: Student makes chocolate bar from entirely British cocoa
item.description: Maha Khan, a master's student in food security at the University of Reading, has created a chocolate bar made entirely from British ingredients, including the cocoa beans themselves. She harvested cocoa pods from the university's greenhouses and combined them with British milk and sugar to produce six bars, named The Reading 100, in honour of the university's centenary. item.title: Bleached coral heals through touch
item.description: Scientists at Stanford have discovered that bleached coral can recover through touch. This insight comes from research into coral restoration and may offer new avenues for preserving coral reefs.

item.title: Maya Higa builds wildlife sanctuary via Twitch
item.description: Maya Higa has established a wildlife sanctuary funded by the people who follow her on Twitch. The nature reserve is known as Alveus Sanctuary. Higa also shared her story during a TED Talk.

item.title: Counterterrorism expert Farah Pandith teaches communities to practice compassion
item.description: Farah Pandith spent decades working in the counterterrorism sector, including for the administrations of Obama, George W. Bush, and George H.W. Bush. She investigated why people fall into ideologies that divide the world into „us versus them," and discovered that extremism often stems from insecurity and a search for recognition or a place in the world. item.title: Beavers return to Loch Ness after 500 years
item.description: After 500 years of absence, beavers are getting a new home around Loch Ness in Scotland. On 30 October, conservation organisation NatureScot granted a licence to the non-profits Trees for Life and Beaver Trust to release up to 15 beaver families over the next three years in the River Ness catchment, of which the loch forms part. item.title: Carbon credits open Great Koala National Park in NSW
item.description: In New South Wales, Australia, carbon credits have played a role in making the Great Koala National Park possible. Further details about the process or background are not provided in the source.

item.title: Xie Junwu Teaches Others Wheelchair Skateboarding in China
item.description: Xie Junwu, a wheelchair athlete from Nanchang, has climbed mountains, run marathons and now skateboards.
